newsitem.title: USA: AOL adding modems to expand network capacity.
newsitem.headline: AOL adding modems to expand network capacity.

text.p: America Online Inc said that it will lease an additional 50,000 modems from outside suppliers so it can expand its network capacity two months ahead of schedule.

AOL said this move is in addition to its ongoing $350 million system expansion program, which it is initiating to answer the "busy signal" problem encountered by its users since it switched to unlimited access for $19.95 a month.
AOL said the new modems, combined with its network expansion, should result in more than 150,000 new modems to serve its members by the end of April.

The supplemental capacity will begin to be deployed by the end of this month. AOL said that the additional capacity will translate into the ability to handle more than 16 million member sessions a day by April, a six million increase over the average level in January.
AOL unveiled the new modem plan with its second quarter earnings.

AOL reported a net loss of $154.8 million, or $1.64 a share, which included an expected $74.3 million related to its October restructuring. AOL also had a one-time charge of about $24 million for estimated credits and refunds that are a result of its recent pact with 36 states attorneys general.

AOL said that its revenues in the quarter jumped to $409.4 million, up 64 percent from $249.1 million a year ago, with record growth in its subscriber base fueled by its flat-rate pricing plan, as well as increased revenues from advertising and electronic commerce.

AOL said its other revenues, including advertising, rose 50 percent on a sequential basis, to a record $58.2 million. Of those revenues, advertising and electronic commerce grew even faster, to $40 million from about $24 million in the previous quarter and up from $13 million a year ago.
AOL said that its unlimited pricing plan has been adopted by over 80 percent of its members, which AOL expects to hold at its current eight million range.

As previously announced, AOL said it plans to manage its membership at its current level until it obtains enough capacity to satisfactorily meet demand. AOL previously said it would be able to meet its demand by June with the new capacity.
"We're delighted to have secured additional modem capacity to serve our members' needs during this period of unprecedented demand," said AOL chief executive officer Steve Case.
"By adding new modems faster, we will accelerate the improvement of access to better serve our members," Case added.

"With this new capacity, we expect to be able to handle around six million more sessions daily by the end of April - two months ahead of schedule - and significantly cut down on the difficulties which our members are experiencing connecting to AOL. We're working day and night to get ahead of demand."
